title: A different kind of fast
description: New materials, new possibilities, and performance without precedent.

cars.name: Porsche Carrera GT
cars.description: The Carrera GT brought racing technology to a road-going Porsche with a carbon-fibre structure, a naturally aspirated V10 and a six-speed manual gearbox. Its removable roof panels and raised gear lever gave the cabin a distinctive character. The sculpted engine cover and clean bodywork expressed a focused approach to supercar design.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent standard 2004 Carrera GT examples. Mileage, originality and specialist maintenance history affect value; modified cars and exceptional provenance are separate considerations.

cars.name: Ferrari Enzo
cars.description: Named after Ferrari’s founder, the Enzo translated competition technology into a dramatic road car. A carbon-fibre chassis, naturally aspirated V12 and paddle-shift transmission sat beneath angular bodywork shaped around aerodynamic performance. Its pointed nose, rising doors and purposeful cabin captured Ferrari’s early-2000s vision of the flagship supercar.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent standard 2003 Enzo road cars. Mileage, service history and provenance can substantially affect individual prices; FXX competition cars are excluded.

cars.name: Ford GT
cars.description: The reborn Ford GT recalled the proportions of the Le Mans-winning GT40 while using modern engineering throughout. A supercharged V8 and six-speed manual gearbox powered the mid-engined coupé. Roof-cut doors, round rear lights and a low, wide stance connected Ford’s racing heritage with the supercar ambitions of a new century.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent standard 2005 GT coupés. Heritage liveries, very low mileage and modifications can change values; the later V6-powered GT is a different generation.

cars.name: Bugatti Veyron 16.4
cars.description: The Veyron combined a quad-turbocharged W16 with all-wheel drive and a carefully finished two-seat cabin. Production began in 2005, bringing Bugatti’s extraordinary engineering project to the road. Its rounded silhouette, horseshoe grille and twin-tone bodywork gave extreme performance a distinctive grand-touring presence rather than a stripped-back racing character.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent standard 2008 Veyron 16.4 coupés. Grand Sport, Super Sport, special editions and exceptional provenance have different values.

cars.name: Audi R8 4.2 FSI quattro
cars.description: Audi’s first production R8 paired a mid-mounted V8 with quattro all-wheel drive and an aluminium structure. The original coupé’s contrasting side blades and low roofline made it instantly recognisable. A driver-focused cabin and available open-gated manual gearbox helped give this everyday-usable sports car a character of its own.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent 2007 4.2 FSI coupés. Transmission, mileage and service history affect value; V10, GT, Spyder and second-generation models are excluded.
